reproductions.notes:
Ruffle executable MD5: 201dde670a7cab019f5f2212bcfbb7b9. Ubuntu 24.04 needs some compatibility work for this old Ruffle build. I extracted Ubuntu's libssl1.1 package locally and launched libTAS with its library path:
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$HOME/TAS/M100005/compat/libssl1.1/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu". I also had to use an Xorg session rather than Wayland (under Wayland, Ruffle either failed to create the graphics surface or hung at frame 1 under libTAS). Ruffle was launched with "-g gl /home/tas2404/TAS/M100005/AmazingDozen.swf" and libTAS was launched with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1. The movie synced for me with the_amazing.swf (renamed to AmazingDozen.swf) with SHA1 8571fe468aa60e9fe0a9e341d516dceb156cab24, MD5 897364148f8eae0a826d340b0df30c0c, size 89384 bytes. P.S. Building libTAS 1.4.3 on Ubuntu 24.04 also required adding missing <cstdint> includes to several old source headers due to the newer GCC toolchain.
